section_summary: This section concerns proposals to sell residual U.S. military surplus in occupied Japan to Japanese civilian agencies through the Foreign Liquidation Commissioner. War Department correspondence divides surplus property into categories A, B, and C, argues that category C sales would reduce custodial and occupation costs and aid economic stabilization, and requests authority for suitable financial arrangements. Later State Department memoranda value the available and anticipated civilian-type surplus at approximately $105 million and recommend conditional authorization while reserving repayment terms and priorities for the Japanese peace settlement.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on payment and policy issues in disposing of military supplies in Japan
subfiles.about: Continuation of an analysis of National Advisory Council policy and the financial and public-policy implications of transferring surplus military goods to Japanese agencies.
subfiles.summary: Council recommends essential supplies in Japan be paid on current import terms, a claim on export proceeds; Royall says some surplus is an unrealizable expense; author urges caution about claims priority, reparations and whether disposal amounts to reparations to Japan.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting financial arrangements for category C surplus sales to Japanese agencies
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.to: W. L. Clayton, Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Royall requests authority for a method of financing transfers of residual category C military surplus to Japanese civilian agencies and individuals.
subfiles.summary: Royall divides surplus into categories A, B and residual C; selling C in Japan avoids custody costs, curbs inflation, supports occupation aims and cuts US-financed imports within limits on Japanese development.

subfiles.title: Forwarding letter transmitting four War Department enclosures
subfiles.from: C. I. Davis, Lieutenant Colonel, GSC
subfiles.about: Davis forwards requested copies of War Department correspondence addressed to Clayton, General Connolly, Harold Glasser, and Norman Ness.
subfiles.summary: Brief letter transmits four enclosures, thanking Schenefield; copies to Clayton, General Connolly, Harold Glasser and N. Ness.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 1: copy of Royall letter to Clayton on category C surplus
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.to: W. L. Clayton, Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: A copy of Royall's request for authority to arrange sales of category C surplus property to Japanese agencies and individuals.
subfiles.summary: This enclosure repeats the classification of Japanese surplus property into categories A, B, and C. It argues that residual items should be sold inside Japan to avoid continuing personnel and custodial costs, assist economic stabilization, and reduce the occupation burden. Royall concludes by requesting authorization for the necessary financial arrangements.

subfiles.from: Office of the Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: An enclosure identified by the forwarding letter as correspondence to General Connolly, although its body is illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Signed copy of Royall letter requesting authority for category C transfers
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.to: W. L. Clayton, Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: A signed copy of the War Department proposal for financially arranging transfers of residual military surplus to Japanese civilian agencies.
subfiles.summary: Royall's signed letter seeks authority for category C transfers, arguing sales in Japan protect US finances, cut personnel and custody costs and ease the occupation burden; NAC action covered only category A.

subfiles.title: Routing slip directing action on Royall's proposal
subfiles.from: W. L. Clayton, Under Secretary for Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Clayton routes the category C surplus matter to Ness for appropriate action.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip directing OFD, specifically Ness, to take action; dated September 5 and stamped September 6, 1946.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Royall's category C request
subfiles.to: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Clayton acknowledges Royall's September 3 request and promises a further communication after consideration of the category C financing question.
subfiles.summary: Clayton acknowledges Royall's category C letter, says it is receiving attention and a further reply will follow.

subfiles.title: Memorandum estimating category C civilian-type surplus property
subfiles.about: Shenefield itemizes the cost valuation of War Department, Navy, and Marine civilian-type surplus available or expected to become available for transfer in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Estimate of category C civilian-type surplus: $45 million now ($39 million War, $6 million Navy and Marine) and $60 million more later, totaling $105 million.

subfiles.title: Memorandum recommending the Departmental position on residual surplus sales in Japan
subfiles.about: Shenefield reports an ad hoc committee's recommended State Department position on transferring residual surplus property in Japan to Japanese agencies.
subfiles.summary: Committee: category C surplus of $45 million now and $60 million later, apart from $15 million for Korea; FLC sales could aid rehabilitation and cut costs; transfers authorized when beneficial, repayment left to the peace conference.
